title: 29 April 1947 — Fundamental Rights Enter the House
summary: The Advisory Committee's interim Fundamental Rights report reaches the Assembly; members debate enforceability, economic rights, restrictions, remedies and begin clause-by-clause consideration.

title: Justiciable vs Non-Justiciable Rights
summary: The House confronts the distinction between rights enforceable through courts and social-economic principles intended to guide legislation and policy.

title: Economic Rights, Caste and Untouchability
summary: P. R. Thakur argues that meaningful rights cannot ignore material inequality and that abolishing untouchability requires confronting the deeper caste structure.

title: Liberty and the Problem of Restrictions
summary: Somnath Lahiri challenges restrictions and emergency qualifications that he sees as giving state power too much room to defeat promised liberties.

title: Constitutional Remedies as Practical Rights
summary: N. G. Ranga stresses that constitutional liberties require protection against authoritarian abuse and meaningful access to judicial remedies, including for poor citizens.

title: Rights of Equality — Detailed Drafting Begins
summary: After the report is taken into consideration, clause-by-clause work reaches equality provisions and turns broad constitutional ideals into legal text.
